title: Plotting scatter graphs
subtitle: Plot and read pairs of numbers on a scatter graph.

questions.prompt: What does one point on a scatter graph show?
questions.correct: One pair of numbers from the table.
questions.feedback: Yes. One number across, one number up.

wrong.label: One number from the table.
wrong.feedback: A point needs two numbers: one across and one up.

wrong.label: The two numbers added together.
wrong.feedback: We don't add them. The point sits at both numbers.

wrong.label: The difference between the two numbers.
wrong.feedback: We don't take them away. The point sits at both numbers.

questions.prompt: How do you read this point?
questions.correct: Go straight down to the bottom axis, then straight across to the side axis.
questions.feedback: Yes. That gives the first number, then the second.

wrong.label: Read the side axis first, then the bottom axis.
wrong.feedback: That gives the pair back to front.

wrong.label: Read the nearest number written on the grid.
wrong.feedback: The point might not sit on a written number. Go down and across to the axes.

wrong.label: Count the points to the left of it.
wrong.feedback: The other points don't matter. Go down and across to the axes.

questions.prompt: Sam plots the pair 6 and 2 by going across to 2 and up to 6. What went wrong?
questions.correct: Sam swapped the numbers. It's across to 6, then up to 2.
questions.feedback: Yes. The first number goes across.

wrong.label: Nothing. The order doesn't matter.
wrong.feedback: Across 2, up 6 is a different place from across 6, up 2.

wrong.label: Sam should have added 6 and 2 first.
wrong.feedback: We never add them. One goes across and one goes up.

wrong.label: Sam should have plotted two points.

questions.prompt: Two pupils both revised for 4 hours. One got a mark of 6 and the other got 8. How do you plot them?
questions.correct: Two points, one above the other, both across at 4.
questions.feedback: Yes. Each pair gets its own point.

wrong.label: One point at 4, halfway between 6 and 8.
wrong.feedback: Each pupil needs their own point.

wrong.label: Just one point, because they both revised for 4 hours.
wrong.feedback: Each pair gets its own point, even if the first numbers match.

wrong.label: Two points side by side along the bottom.
wrong.feedback: Both go across to 4, so one sits above the other.

questions.prompt: On this side axis, what is one square worth?
questions.feedback: Yes. Two squares make 20, so one square is 10.

wrong.feedback: That's the gap between two numbers. There are two squares in that gap.
Squares aren't always worth 1. Count the squares between two numbers.
2 is how many squares there are between numbers, not what each one is worth.

points.text: A scatter graph shows pairs of numbers as points.
Each point is one pair: the first number goes across, the second goes up.
To read a point, go straight down to the bottom axis, then straight across to the side axis.
Two pairs that start with the same number get two points, one above the other.
Before you read or plot, find what one square is worth.
